payload.text: Can’t you just read logs and see what happened?

context.scope: cluster connection warnings during the recorded rollout
context.earlier_reply: Brief startup connection warnings stopped appearing in the latest checked logs; rollout completion is still pending.

observations.observation: Both old application nodes logged unable to connect to .103 at 18:51:26–57 during rollout. New .103 later passes readiness; cluster membership still requires recheck. Fleet has 16 connected runners and zero pending dispatch at 18:51:19.

replacement-a starts 18:52:05, reports migrations already up 18:52:08, connects old .101/.102 at 18:52:13 and starts HTTP at 18:52:18. It warns unable to connect to second replacement .104 at 18:55:16, 18:55:46 and 18:56:17. No later cluster/application WARNING/ERROR or Sent 5xx matches through 19:04:53; bounded read untruncated.

replacement-b .104 application starts 18:56:25, migrations already up 18:56:27, connects .101 and replacement-a .103 at 18:56:32 and starts HTTP at 18:56:35. No cluster/application WARNING/ERROR or Sent 5xx matches in its startup journal through 19:04:53; bounded read untruncated. Earlier .104 warnings occurred before its application process started, and successful connection afterward establishes startup timing rather than persistent cluster failure.

quality_rubric.criterion: Explains the warning with the recorded sequence: connection attempts preceded replacement startup and successful cluster joins followed; supports a startup gap rather than persistent cluster failure.
Names relevant timestamps and distinguishes the historical cause from current health. Does not treat a quiet recent window alone as the cause.
Keeps the conclusion within the recorded log window; does not claim zero downtime, no future failures, or authenticated sign-in verification.
